a systematic and model-independent analysis of the DM properties in a generic framework of inflationary cosmology.
the model-independent constraints on DM properties from the initial condition set by the inflaton decay, and the implications for various DM searches.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the inflaton decay to thermal DM is strongly disfavoured, and non-thermal DM can be realised in a large region of parameter space, with the caveat that it is difficult to construct a realistic model of inflation and reheating in such a scenario.

the inflaton decay to a thermal DM species is disfavored for a large range parameter space, while the non-thermal scenario is allowed in a large parameter region, and the thermal scenario is allowed in the freeze-out and freeze-in regions of DM parameter space.

, for a given DM model, it is possible to obtain the correct DM relic density only in the narrow region where the DM annihilation cross-section falls in between the standard freeze-out and freeze-in regions, or in the non-thermal region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-thermal scenario is the most generic one, and the thermal scenario is only viable for DM masses in a very limited range, which is constrained by a number of cosmological observables.

for a given DM mass, the thermal freeze-out region is constrained by the unitarity limit and the Planck data, while the thermal freeze-in region is constrained by indirect DM search experiments and the Planck measurements.
the non-thermal and freeze-in regions are allowed only for DM masses below a few keV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the initial abundance of the DM is a crucial factor in determining its final abundance, and hence its properties, which must be taken into consideration when constructing DM models.
the DM abundance is set by a combination of the initial conditions and the subsequent evolution of DM, which must be accounted for in any model building.
the non-thermal nature of the DM abundance, if present, can be probed by the upcoming CMB and LSS experiments, and thus must be taken into consideration while interpreting their results.
